paper.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? From Noisy Teacher to Self-Improvement
paper.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) offers dense token-level supervision but teacher scores are noisy. Our analysis reveals that learning concentrates on low log-probability tokens, suggesting OPD works largely by suppressing tail tokens rather than transferring teacher knowledge. Motivated by this, we propose OPSA, a supervision-free method using entropy-adaptive negative advantages, which improves AIME24 Avg@32 by 35.41 points over the base model without any teacher.

paper.title: DreamX-Creator: Democratizing Native Audio-Video Generation at 2K Resolution
paper.summary: We present a compact 7B native joint audio-video generator using Gated Cross-Modal Attention and progressive joint training. It achieves synchronized high-resolution output through Audio-Video Reinforcement Learning with modality-aware feedback, and an autoregressive 1-step 2K refinement pipeline enables efficient single-pass generation.

paper.title: Lucida: Parse, Generate, and Place for Composable Real-to-Sim Scene Modeling
paper.summary: Scene reconstruction is reformulated as parsing, asset generation, and VLM-guided placement. A GizmoAct policy manipulates object gizmos via multi-turn GUI interaction. Lucida improves mAP by 69% over Boxer and raises ADD-SB@0.05 from 57.8% to 83.4% on benchmarks.

paper.title: GenFirst: Generation Before Reconstruction for Stable End-to-End Latent Generative Modeling
paper.summary: Direct end-to-end training of latent generative models collapses; we show entropy preservation in the KL objective avoids it. A generation-first strategy shapes latent space under weak reconstruction pressure before strengthening recovery, achieving gFID 0.97 on ImageNet-256 and GenEval 0.90 on text-to-image.

paper.title: Normalized Low-Rank Adaptation
paper.summary: NoRA normalizes the down-projection matrices in LoRA training to stabilize early optimization dynamics. It improves convergence, performance, and training stability across pretraining, supervised finetuning, and reinforcement learning without extra parameters or inference cost.

paper.title: PaperGym: Rubric-Centered Evolution for Research-Plan Generation
paper.summary: PaperGym converts scientific papers into training environments by separating research questions from evaluation rubrics derived from methods and experiments. An OPSD self-teacher with GRPO training improves Qwen3-8B to 73.48 on ResearchQA, outperforming larger models on research planning tasks.

paper.title: On the Design of Qwen3.8-Next Architecture: Evaluation, Efficiency, and Training Stability
paper.summary: A sparse mixture-of-experts model with 125B parameters and 6B activated per token combines Gated DeltaNet, Qwen Sparse Attention, and gated residual branches. It matches a larger predecessor at 1/3 parameters, 1/3 training tokens, and 1/9 training FLOPs, and we report training stability findings.

paper.title: CogEvol: Towards Efficient and Reliable Learning Environment Generation
paper.summary: CogEvol generates structured learning artifacts (slides, interactive pages) in a single pass using SFT and GRPO with vision-language rewards, completing slides in 17 seconds median and interactive pages in 59 seconds with 26.9x fewer parameters than multi-turn agent scaffolding.

paper.title: LightNav-0: Eliciting VLM Spatial Intelligence for Generalist Embodied Navigation
paper.summary: A compact model leverages vision-language model spatial reasoning via unified pointing tokens and a vector-quantized action tokenizer. It achieves state-of-the-art across 10 navigation benchmarks with zero-shot generalization to diverse robot embodiments, scenes, and targets.

paper.title: Evaluating the Hidden Costs of Personalization in Large Language Models
paper.summary: We introduce PRISK, a framework revealing how personalized context increases irrelevant personalization, preference narrowing, and sycophantic bias. Across 13 LLMs, user profiles and retrieved memories exacerbate biases with average drops of 45.9%, 41.7%, and 61.7%.
